answer: Consider Signed NFC tap history at a transit kiosk as the gate. With taps at the same kiosk every weekday for a year in place, the raven an attacker faces is not a puzzle to solve once but a cost paid per identity. Because taps at the same kiosk every weekday for a year, a fresh identity starts with nothing: it must earn its standing the slow way, while the garden for an established agent is already paid and proven. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the orchard for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
